_note: one entry for each placeholder @@...@@ of the post, keyed by its exact words: value, unit, a text for the page, and how it was computed. Losses are held-out losses in nats per token at the end of training. A rung of the ladder is the mean of its two seeds; the swaps and the warmup runs are one seed each. The seed yardstick: the two seeds of a rung differ by 0.001 to 0.018 nats over the 10 rungs of the ladder: 0.006 or less on 8 of them, 0.015 on RMS norm without parameters and 0.018 on the 2019 recipe; root mean square 0.008. A difference between two single runs under 0.016 is inside seed noise, 0.024 or more is clear, between the two it is at the edge. The swaps are single runs at 50M tokens, where no pair of seeds was run, so the yardstick is borrowed from the ladder (100M tokens). Numbers are rounded to six significant digits first, as in the files the figures read.

gradient norm of the MLP output matrix a.note: gptpp.export.gradient_by_depth: the 2019 recipe at width 256, 8 random initializations a cell, one batch of 8 x 256 held-out tokens; the Frobenius norm of the gradient of each block's second MLP matrix, averaged over the seeds, last block over first block. Post-norm does NOT rise toward the output; pre-norm falls toward it. results_lines.Section 5.2, where the norm sits: whethe: No. At initialization post-norm is level, not rising: under GPT-2's initialization every block but the first receives the same gradient (0.079 at 48 blocks; the first, which reads the raw embedding, 0.94), and with Glorot weights the two ends differ by at most 23% and in no steady direction (1.35 to 1.58 at 12 blocks, 1.41 to 1.53 at 24 blocks, 1.99 to 1.53 at 48 blocks). Pre-norm is the one with a slope, and it falls toward the output: 3.59 to 1.25 at 48 blocks under GPT-2's initialization, 1.31 to 0.27 with Glorot weights, as its stream grows (1.14 to 6.62). The top-layer gradient with depth agrees with Proposition 5.2.5 in its own setting (Glorot weights): from 12 to 48 blocks it changes by a factor 0.94 for post-norm and 0.47 for pre-norm (1/sqrt(4) = 0.50); under GPT-2's initialization, whose 1/sqrt(2L) makes the pre-norm stream end at the same size at every depth (0.088, 0.088, 0.088), it does not change in either (1.00, 1.01). Training at 8 layers, the 2019 recipe, 50M tokens, one seed each, in steps of 8,192 tokens at rate 0.0006 (the warmup of 8M tokens is 977 steps): pre-norm 4.581 with a warmup and 4.950 without; post-norm 4.537 with a warmup and 7.696 without. With a warmup post-norm trains and is 0.044 ahead; without one it collapses to token frequencies (for scale, token frequencies alone give 7.70 on held-out text (the unigram level of part 8's replayed run) and a uniform guess over the 32,768 tokens 10.40) where pre-norm loses 0.37. At the ladder's step of 65,536 tokens and rate 0.0024, where the same warmup is 122 steps, post-norm collapsed to token frequencies with a warmup too (7.690, 7.690), within 40 steps and pre-norm reached 4.613 and 5.706: those two post-norm runs are a collapse, not evidence about warmup, and nothing here says that post-norm cannot train. In the 2026 recipe (Muon, writers at zero, 50M tokens) post-norm trains too: 4.133 against 4.026 for the same layer norm placed before the sublayers.
results_lines.Section 5.2, which norm: whether layer n: Layer norm (4.026) and RMS norm with a gain (4.025) are within 0.001 of each other: centering does not matter. Both are better than the parameter-free RMS norm of the recipe (4.045), by 0.019 and 0.020: at the edge of seed noise (between 0.016 and 0.024 for two single runs): probably real, not settled by one seed. On the ladder, where a rung is the mean of two seeds, the same step (rung 3, layer norm with its gain to parameter-free RMS norm) cost +0.031 (+0.026 in one seed, +0.037 in the other): the learned gain helps at this size. Dynamic tanh lands at 4.077, +0.031 (worse by more than seed noise). Without normalization the model does not train even with zero-initialized projections: the loss was 5.98 at step 70 and not finite at step 80. One seed each for the swaps.
results_lines.Section 5.3, the activations: the order: Lowest to highest loss: SwiGLU 4.037, GeGLU 4.043, squared ReLU 4.045, GELU 4.046, SiLU 4.052, ReLU 4.063. One run each, so the order is not a ranking. Against squared ReLU, inside seed noise (under 0.016): SwiGLU −0.008, GeGLU −0.002, GELU +0.001, SiLU +0.007; at the edge: ReLU +0.018; clear (0.024 or more): none. The second-order units average 4.042 and the first-order ones 4.054: 0.012 apart, mostly ReLU's doing; GELU ties squared ReLU. The 0.02 to 0.05 of the literature is not there at 8 layers and 50M tokens: close to a null result. What does differ is what the units do: 83% of squared ReLU's activations and 86% of ReLU's are exact zeros, GELU has 1%; the kurtosis of the activations is 1306 for squared ReLU, 289 and 306 for the two gated units and 43 for GELU; dead units are rare in all six: none in 5 of them and 0.03% of the units at most (relu2).
results_lines.Section 5.4, neurons as memories: whethe: In part. The share of a neuron's 25 strongest triggers that end in its commonest last token is highest in block 2 (0.41) and lowest in block 12 (0.26); random positions give 0.08. Lower layers are the more shallow, as in the 2021 table, but by a modest margin. The top token of a value is the token after its key's strongest trigger for 1% of the neurons of block 1, 13% in block 9 and 5% in block 12 (chance 0.003%): values continue their triggers in the upper half, not at the very top. Coefficients are non-negative (squared ReLU). 200 neurons sampled a block, the 25 strongest triggers of each.
results_lines.Section 5.5, the initializations: whethe: Only two of the three were run. With the writers scaled by 1/sqrt(2L) the 2026 recipe ends at 4.0438, with the writers at zero at 4.0451: 0.0013 apart, inside seed noise. During training the two cross: −0.010 at 10M tokens, +0.010 at 20M tokens (scaled less zero). No difference at the end and none that lasts early, at 8 layers. Plain 0.02 on every matrix was not run, so the sources' claim that the scaled rule clearly beats it is untested here. On the ladder, under AdamW at 100M tokens, zero writers were −0.027 against the scaled rule (−0.025 in one seed, −0.030 in the other): there the change is clear.
results_lines.Section 5.6, the table: the swaps that c: The 2026 recipe with one old part put back (50M tokens, one seed each; inside seed noise under 0.016, clear from 0.024). The rows of the post's table that cost the most: learned positions +0.112, no query-key normalization +0.029. Every swap run, by standing. Clear, the old part costs: pos-none +0.264, sched-constant +0.150, pos-sinusoidal +0.133, pos-learned +0.112, norm-post +0.088, pos-sinusoidal-after-norm +0.060, attn-mqa +0.050, norm-dyt +0.031, sched-cosine +0.031, attn-gqa2 +0.030, attn-no-qk-norm +0.029, and without normalization the run diverged. At the edge: act-relu +0.018, norm-layernorm −0.019, norm-rmsnorm-gain −0.020, bias −0.021. Inside seed noise: no-embed-norm +0.014, sched-linear +0.011, act-silu +0.007, attn-gqa4 +0.003, pos-alibi +0.002, attn-qk-learned +0.001, act-gelu +0.001, tied 0.000, init-gpt2 −0.001, act-geglu −0.002, no-softcap −0.002, act-swiglu −0.008, no-warmup −0.008. Clear, the old part is better: none. The full 2019 recipe ends at 4.135 and the full 2026 recipe at 3.814 (the ladder, 100M tokens, means of two seeds): a gap of 0.321, of which the training recipe of 2026 (rung 7: Muon on the hidden matrices, with its rates and its schedule) is 0.155 (48%) and the eight changes to the block 0.165 (52%); rotary positions alone are 0.110. Rung by rung, the step of the means and of each seed: no biases 0.000 (−0.010 in one seed, +0.010 in the other), rotary positions −0.110 (−0.111 in one seed, −0.110 in the other), RMS norm without parameters +0.031 (+0.026 in one seed, +0.037 in the other), squared ReLU −0.033 (−0.022 in one seed, −0.043 in the other), QK normalization −0.011 (−0.016 in one seed, −0.007 in the other), zero-initialized writers −0.027 (−0.025 in one seed, −0.030 in the other), the training recipe of 2026 −0.155 (−0.157 in one seed, −0.154 in the other), untied tables with a normalized embedding −0.011 (−0.012 in one seed, −0.010 in the other), the soft cap −0.003 (+0.000 in one seed, −0.006 in the other). At 8 layers and 50M tokens three simplifications of the 2026 block measure slightly worse than what they replaced: layer norm with its gain put back is 0.019 better, RMS norm with a gain 0.020, biases 0.021; one seed each, at the edge of seed noise (between 0.016 and 0.024 for two single runs): probably real, not settled by one seed (the largest difference seen between the two seeds of a rung is 0.018; the three rungs trained with Muon differ by 0.0035 at most). GELU ties squared ReLU (+0.001). On the ladder, removing the biases is worth nothing (−0.0001 on the means: −0.010 in one seed, +0.010 in the other), and the parameter-free norm costs +0.031 (+0.026 in one seed, +0.037 in the other). What is clear: rotary positions (+0.112 with a learned table), the training recipe of 2026 (−0.155 on the ladder), query-key normalization (+0.029 without) and pre-norm (+0.088 with post-norm and layer norm, +0.107 against the same layer norm before the sublayers). The norm on the embedding: +0.014 without it (inside seed noise), 0.000 when it goes together with the second vocabulary matrix (the tied run, 16.8M parameters fewer). The ladder and the swaps ask different questions and twice give different answers: squared ReLU gained 0.033 on the ladder (−0.022 in one seed, −0.043 in the other; under AdamW, right after the norm lost its gain) and GELU put back into the finished recipe costs +0.001; writers at zero gained 0.027 on the ladder (−0.025 in one seed, −0.030 in the other) and the scaled rule put back costs −0.001. Query-key normalization goes the other way: −0.011 on the ladder (−0.016 in one seed, −0.007 in the other), +0.029 when taken out of the finished recipe. Rung 7 taken apart in seed 0: of the 0.157 nats, 0.074 is the rest of the training recipe and 0.083 Muon in place of AdamW (the 2026 training recipe with AdamW at its better rate ends at 3.911).
